subject: WarpDrive SDK migration & endpoint cutover sprint plan
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@parkline.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightpay.io>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: WarpDrive migration window and requirements

Karthik — thanks again for the demo last week. Parkline is ready to move forward with the WarpDrive integration for our fraud-inspection pipeline. Before we lock dates with infra, we need a concrete migration runbook and clear guidance on:

- SDK upgrade steps (current v1.8 -> v2.0)
- Endpoint migration strategy (staged cutover vs switch-and-roll-back)
- Recommended timeouts / retry backoff for our real-time paths (99th p50 targets)
- Rate-limit handling and how the SDK surfaces quota errors

Can your team share a proposed sprint plan and any sample snippets we should start testing?

Ideal timeline: start sandbox cutover the week of July 9, production switch July 23. Let me know if that aligns with your bandwidth.

—Samir
Parkline, Senior Engineering Manager
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@parkline.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: WarpDrive migration window and requirements

Samir — thanks, this is helpful. We can absolutely support the July timeline; below is a high-level sprint plan and the attachments include a detailed runbook and sample snippets. Quick summary:

Sprint plan (high level)
- Week 1 (sandbox prep): SDK v2.0 drop-in + integration smoke tests, set up request-level tracing
- Week 2 (sandbox cutover): traffic split 10/90 -> 50/50 -> 90/10 over three days, validate latency and error budget
- Week 3 (stabilize): expand test coverage, rollback playbook rehearsal, retries/backoff tuning
- Week 4 (prod migration): 1-hour maintenance window + gradual ramp if rollback metrics clear

Key recommendations (summary)
- SDK: use the new connection pool api; sample in sdk-sample-snippets-v2.zip. The v2.0 client includes an opt-in adaptive backoff mode (recommended for bursty workloads).
- Endpoint migration: we recommend staged split testing (traffic mirroring -> split -> ramp). Switch-and-roll-back is riskier for stateful caching.
- Timeouts/retries: per-request timeout = 3s baseline for sync calls, 1.2s for the fastest path with streaming. Retries: at most 3 attempts with exponential jittered backoff (200ms -> 800ms -> 1600ms). Use idempotency keys for safety.
- Rate-limit handling: SDK surfaces 429s via a RateLimitError type and exposes token bucket state via the client metrics endpoint. We can push a small helper that automatically honors Retry-After when present.

Attachments: warpdrive-migration-runbook.pdf (full checklist), sdk-sample-snippets-v2.zip (examples + terraform).

I'll loop in Vanessa for SRE coordination and Grace for CS handoff notes. If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute runbook walkthrough this week.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@parkline.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: WarpDrive migration window and requirements

Samir — adding a few operational clarifications from the SRE side:

- Observability: enable token-level tracing in sandbox to correlate client retries with Redwood route logs. We recommend a 72-hour retention for the migration window.
- Circuit breaker: set error-rate threshold at 5% over a 5-minute window to trigger failover to the existing endpoint. We will provide a pre-built policy in the runbook.
- Cache priming: for prefix/KV caching pay attention to cold-starts — plan a 2-hour warmup after each traffic ramp.

Also note that our adaptive backoff in v2 respects server-sent Retry-After headers and will back off faster when your account hits quota tiers. We'll add a short snippet to the runbook that shows how to read client-side rate bucket metrics (prometheus format).

Vanessa Ortiz
Technical Program Manager, Integrations
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightpay.io>

Date: Tue, 26 Jun 2028 08:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: WarpDrive migration window and requirements

Thanks — quick Q on the retry strategy. Parkline's payments path is latency-sensitive; our engineers are worried that 3 retries at the long backoff will push transactions beyond SLAs. Any guidance on tailoring a shorter retry window for the 1.2s fast path?

Also, can the SDK surface a non-blocking retry that returns an optimistic fallback for non-critical requests?

—Elena
Lead Platform Engineer, BrightPay (Parkline partner)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightpay.io>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Shah <samir.shah@parkline.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 26 Jun 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: WarpDrive migration window and requirements

Elena — good questions. Two practical options for latency-sensitive paths:

1) Short-retry profile (recommended for payment API)
- Per-request timeout: 900ms
- Retries: 1 attempt only, backoff 150ms -> stop. Use a synchronous fast path.
- Use idempotency and dedicated routing to a lower-latency instance pool.

2) Non-blocking fallback (best-effort)
- Fire-and-forget variant: the SDK returns immediately with a local optimistic response and emits the actual token to an async queue for reconciliation. Useful for enrichment or non-critical scoring. Not recommended for payments.

We included a code sample in sdk-sample-snippets-v2.zip called fast-path.md that shows how to configure the client: setRetryProfile({maxAttempts:1, baseMs:150, timeoutMs:900}) and enable optimisticFallback: true for chosen calls. We'll also attach a short benchmark that shows p50/p99 impact across profiles.

If Parkline wants, we can add a patch to your sandbox (small feature flag) so you can toggle the retry profile and run a 48-hour heat test before prod.

-Karthik
